summary: Register row 'Turbine 1' (13 MWe, COD 1996, operator AMK) is a turbine unit at the Iserlohn waste-to-energy plant (MHKW, Giesestrasse), operated by AMK mbH, which is 51% owned by the Maerkischer Kreis and 49% by EDG Holding and Lobbe via MK Beteiligungsgesellschaft. EDG plans to exit by end 2027; no financing, permit tonnage (c.105,000 t/yr burned per press, not a permit figure) or date of the minority partners' entry was found.

parent_owner: E.ON SE (via E.ON Energy Projects GmbH)
heat_offtaker: UPM Hürth-Knapsack paper mill (steam; mill closure announced 2024)

owners.owner: GSH Green Steam Hürth GmbH, 100% subsidiary of E.ON Energy Projects GmbH (E.ON SE)
owners.note: E.ON built and operates the plant on the UPM mill site; owner since project start (construction began Oct 2020). Wolff & Müller release names GSH as client and a subsidiary of E.ON Energy Projects GmbH; an E.ON job advert says 100% subsidiary.

owners.owner: E.ON SE (ultimate parent)
owners.note: Global Energy Monitor, citing MaStR, lists E.ON SE as 100% parent of GSH Green Steam Hürth GmbH.

issues.summary: A crack was found in the fuel bunker during commissioning and the boiler stood idle for five weeks until it was sealed and a structural engineer approved restart. Commissioning was originally planned for Q1 2022.
issues.source_ref: https://www.contextcrew.de/e-on-nimmt-in-huerth-biomassekraftwerk-in-betrieb/ (teaser visible, article paywalled; also EUWID Recycling 19.01.2024, paywalled)

issues.summary: EUWID reported the plant still not at full load because of technical difficulties, with the turbine expected fully in service by end of June 2024.

UPM announced closure of the Hürth-Knapsack paper mill (steam customer, over 130 jobs) by end of 2024; E.ON said it was assessing the impact and still planned commercial operation. Current steam offtake after closure not found.

summary: E.ON-owned 20 MWe wood-fired CHP built on the UPM Hürth-Knapsack site; MaStR shows in operation since 2023-09-15, matching the register row (location is confidential in MaStR; Hürth confirmed from other sources, no postcode found). Main risk is loss of the UPM paper mill steam customer after its announced 2024 closure; acquisition date, financing and the post-closure heat offtaker were not found.

parent_owner: REMONDIS (49%), Wirtschaftsbetriebe Duisburg AöR (City of Duisburg, c.36%), Stadtwerke Oberhausen GmbH via STOAG (City of Oberhausen, c.15%)

owners.owner: REMONDIS
owners.note: Private partner in the GMVA PPP. Percentage is from a 2014 EUWID report on the 2013 WBD accounts; the GMVA website confirms the same three partners today but gives no percentages, so the split may have changed.

owners.owner: Wirtschaftsbetriebe Duisburg AöR (City of Duisburg)
owners.note: c.36% per EUWID 25 Jun 2014 (WBD 2013 annual report); WBD wrote down its GMVA holding by EUR 37.7m in 2013. Current stake not confirmed.

owners.owner: Stadtwerke Oberhausen GmbH (City of Oberhausen, via STOAG)
owners.note: 15% per EUWID 2014. City of Oberhausen press release of 4 Nov 2013 confirms the three shareholders (Oberhausen via STOAG, WBD Duisburg, Remondis) without percentages. Current stake not confirmed.

issues.summary: Automatic fire alarm triggered in a waste bunker, with heavy smoke and an odour nuisance warning to residents; extinguished around 20:00 and police investigating the cause.

Fire in a storage hall at the plant; a 63-year-old employee lost consciousness after driving an excavator out of the burning hall and was taken to hospital. The headline reports he died. Exact day in July 2021 not shown (EUWID issue 30/2021, dated 27 Jul 2021).

Court cases and a regional-government price review over plant sizing and incineration prices put GMVA's liquidity at risk; shareholders created an extra company for municipal waste at a lower price of EUR 159.80 per tonne, and the cities deferred receivables. Duisburg's WBD wrote down its holding by EUR 37.7m in 2013.

summary: Row is one turbine set (25.6 MWe, Turbosatz 1) at the GMVA Niederrhein waste-to-energy plant in Oberhausen (up to 700kt/yr, PPP of Oberhausen, Duisburg and REMONDIS); the operator is the owning company, not a contractor. Shareholder percentages date from 2014 and the acquisition date is not found; no financing found; fires in 2021 and 2025 recorded.

parent_owner: enercity AG (via Danpower GmbH)

owners.owner: Vattenfall Europe New Energy GmbH (via Vattenfall Europe New Energy Ecopower GmbH)
owners.note: Built and operated the plant, in operation since 2010. Sale to Danpower signed 21 Aug 2025, closing expected autumn 2025 subject to Bundeskartellamt clearance; the closing date was not found, so the end date is left blank.

owners.owner: Danpower GmbH (100% subsidiary of enercity AG, Hannover)
owners.note: Buyer under contracts signed 21 Aug 2025. The MaStR register row already lists Danpower as operator, which suggests the sale has closed, but no closing announcement was found. Danpower is a 100% enercity subsidiary per the law firm advisor's release.

issues.summary: The 2023 emissions report lists several unplanned shutdowns: tube damage (5-10 Mar, 14-17 Jun, 30 Aug-3 Sep), grate damage (9-16 Jan, 7-9 Sep), an evaporator fault (13-14 Jul) and a short outage for rust damage repair (10-23 Nov). No waste was processed during these periods.

The BImSchG permit for the plant was only granted retroactively on 11 Jan 2024 (max. firing heat 95.7 MW), although the plant had been operating since 2010. The article is behind a paywall; only the opening paragraph was readable.

summary: EfW CHP at Ost-West-Strasse 25, Rostock (c.175kt/yr, c.18MWe per sale release versus 22.4MW in the register), built by Vattenfall and sold to Danpower (100% enercity) with contracts signed Aug 2025; closing date and price not found. Several unplanned outages in 2023; no financing found.

parent_owner: MVV Energie AG
heat_offtaker: InfraLeuna steam network (process steam) and Merseburg district heating

owners.owner: MVV Umwelt Asset GmbH (100% subsidiary of MVV Energie AG, Mannheim)
owners.note: InfraLeuna company profile states the TREA Leuna site entity is a 100% subsidiary of MVV Energie AG. Original project company was MVV TREA Leuna GmbH; the plant was built under a lease structure (see financing).

financing.borrower: Hannover Leasing subsidiary (lessor), leasing the plant to MVV TREA Leuna GmbH
financing.lender: Landesbank Hessen-Thueringen Girozentrale and KfW IPEX-Bank
financing.instrument: Combined project and leasing finance for the new Leuna waste incineration plant; MVV has an option to buy the plant when the lease ends
financing.refi_basis: Article gives the EUR 94m investment volume but no date or lease term. Whether it covers line I only (2005) or both lines is not stated, and whether MVV has since bought out the lease is unknown.

summary: TREA Leuna line II (commissioned May 2007, 2 x c.20 MWe site total, 390kt/yr) is operated by MVV Umwelt Asset GmbH, a 100% MVV Energie AG subsidiary; the register row is a unit of a two-line site at Leuna, 06237. Acquisition date of the current entity, the lease term and any operating incidents were not found.

parent_owner: FES Frankfurter Entsorgungs- und Service GmbH (City of Frankfurt 51%, Remondis 49%) and Mainova AG, 50:50
heat_offtaker: Mainova district heating network (Nordweststadt, Riedberg, Eschersheim, Bockenheim, Campus Westend)

owners.owner: MHKW Müllheizkraftwerk Frankfurt am Main GmbH, owned 50:50 by FES Frankfurter Entsorgungs- und Service GmbH and Mainova AG
owners.note: Operating company since 1 Oct 2006; shareholders hold equal shares. FES is 51% City of Frankfurt and 49% Remondis per a search result (snippet only). Date is when the operating company took over, not a sale.

owners.owner: FES Frankfurter Entsorgungs- und Service GmbH: City of Frankfurt 51%, Remondis AG & Co. KG 49%
owners.note: Ownership of FES, one of the two shareholders; seen in a search result only. Confirm on fes-frankfurt.de.

issues.summary: Automatic shutdown of the plant after a fault between the plant and the transformer station; Mainova reported a district heat temperature drop in Nordweststadt, Riedberg and Mertonviertel and the plant was restarted the same morning.
Mainova cut district heat to Nordweststadt for c.30 hours on 17/18 Aug and 7/8 Sep 2024 for urgent works at the waste heat plant (c.1,250 connections).
Regierungspraesidium Darmstadt approved permanent four-line operation and raised the annual limit from 525,600 to 660,000 tonnes, with automated bunker cranes.

summary: Row is 'Turbine 7' (75 MWe, COD 1986, from MaStR) at the Frankfurt Nordweststadt EfW CHP, which the operator states has 49 MWe turbine capacity in total, so the register capacity does not match the plant and may be a unit or gross figure; owned 50:50 by FES (Frankfurt/Remondis) and Mainova. No financing found; the plant was rebuilt 1984 to 1987 and 2003 to 2009, and the date the current ownership began (2006 operating company) is not a sale date.

parent_owner: Rethmann SE & Co. KG (via REMONDIS SE & Co. KG)
heat_offtaker: Industrial users on the REMONDIS Lippewerk site (site electricity and steam supply)

owners.owner: Vereinigte Aluminium-Werke AG (VAW)
owners.note: VAW ran the aluminium works at the Lippewerk site from 1938 to 1990 and built the circulating fluidised bed power plant there.

owners.owner: Rethmann SE & Co. KG (via REMONDIS SE & Co. KG; operator REMONDIS Production GmbH)
owners.note: Lippewerk has belonged to the Rethmann waste division since 1993, now REMONDIS. Wikipedia states REMONDIS SE & Co. KG is wholly owned by Rethmann SE & Co. KG. The exact legal holding chain down to REMONDIS Production GmbH was not checked in the Handelsregister.

issues.summary: Bezirksregierung Arnsberg published an exemption under 17. BImSchV (waste incineration ordinance) for the fluidised bed combustion plant of REMONDIS Production GmbH at Brunnenstrasse 138, Lünen. The exemption is a routine permit item, not a breach.

A search summary mentions a turbine defect at the circulating fluidised bed power plant (c. 2012) after water entered a component and caused rust; steam was vented through an emergency valve and safety systems worked as designed. Date and details not confirmed.
issues.source_ref: WebSearch result summary for 'Remondis Lippewerk Wirbelschichtkraftwerk Lünen Störung' (Ruhr Nachrichten / Lokalkompass items, not opened)

summary: The register row is the REMONDIS Lippewerk circulating fluidised bed waste-fired power plant in Lünen, operated by REMONDIS Production GmbH and owned within the Rethmann/REMONDIS group since 1993; the site also has a separate biomass power plant, and the 10.35 MWe row may cover only one unit. No financing found; the 2020 and 2022 fires at the Lippewerk were in recycling halls, not the power plant, and a c. 2012 turbine defect is only an unverified lead.

parent_owner: MVV Energie AG
heat_offtaker: InfraLeuna chemical park steam network; Merseburg district heating

owners.owner: MVV Umwelt Asset GmbH (100% subsidiary of MVV Energie AG)
owners.note: Operator and current owner-operator of TREA Leuna, commissioned 2005. The InfraLeuna company profile states the company is a 100 percent subsidiary of MVV Energie AG. Original build used a lease structure (see financing), so legal title to the plant may have sat with a Hannover Leasing vehicle, with MVV holding a purchase option; current title not confirmed.

financing.borrower: Hannover Leasing subsidiary (lessor), leasing the plant to MVV TREA Leuna GmbH
financing.lender: Landesbank Hessen-Thüringen Girozentrale (Helaba) and KfW IPEX-Bank
financing.instrument: Combined project and leasing finance for the plant build; MVV has an option to buy the plant when the lease ends
financing.refi_basis: Lease term and loan maturity not found; original construction finance for a EUR 94m investment, built c.2003 to 2005
financing.note: Article gives EUR 94m as the investment volume, not the loan amount, and no date. Likely historic and possibly already repaid or replaced.

issues.summary: The Saxony-Anhalt state authority (LVwA) inspected the plant on 31 July 2025 because of an event with environmental impact. No defects were found and no measures were ordered. The nature of the event is not stated.
issues.source_ref: LVwA Sachsen-Anhalt Ueberwachungsbericht, MVV Umwelt Asset GmbH TREA Leuna, site visit 31.07.2025, published 28.11.2025

summary: TREA Leuna (EfW, c.390kt/yr nominal, commissioned 2005) is run by MVV Umwelt Asset GmbH, a 100% subsidiary of MVV Energie AG, and matches the register row (the row has no locality; site is An der B91, Tor 12, Leuna). The 2025 inspections found no defects; the date MVV took ownership, current title (lease structure) and any current debt were not found.

parent_owner: Stadt Solingen (via Technische Betriebe Solingen)
heat_offtaker: Solingen municipal district heating network

owners.owner: Stadtwerke Solingen (first operator)
owners.note: Plant started 9 July 1969 under Stadtwerke Solingen; the earlier-found wording of a November 1969 transfer to the city comes from a search summary only, so the exact date is uncertain. Operating responsibility later moved to EntsorgungsBetriebe Solingen (late 1990s) and then Technische Betriebe Solingen (2011).

owners.owner: Stadt Solingen, operated by Technische Betriebe Solingen (municipal body similar to an own-operation company)
owners.note: Wikipedia lists owner and operator as Technische Betriebe Solingen, which is a municipal institution of the City of Solingen. Register row names Stadt Solingen as operator. The row is one turbine (5.3 MWe) of three at the Muellheizkraftwerk Solingen.

issues.summary: Major fire damaged waste boiler 3 at the plant, which ran at about half capacity during repairs; waste treatment, district heat and power continued thanks to redundant systems.
Boiler 3 returned to service after about a year; repair cost c. EUR 5.5m, covered by insurance, and the plant is back at full load.
Bezirksregierung Duesseldorf environmental inspection found no defects and no measures required.
issues.source_ref: Bezirksregierung Duesseldorf Umweltinspektionsbericht SG-011, inspection 2025-06-10, published 2025-07-21

summary: The row is one steam turbine (5.3 MWe, 1969) at the municipal Muellheizkraftwerk Solingen, Sandstrasse 16a, owned and operated by Technische Betriebe Solingen for the City of Solingen; plant is real and operating after a Nov 2023 boiler fire repaired by Dec 2024. No financing found; exact ownership transfer date and permit tonnage (c. 140,000 t/yr burned) not confirmed.

parent_owner: Evergreen Privatstiftung (via HS Timber Group)
heat_offtaker: Kodersdorf sawmill (timber drying)

owners.owner: Klausner Group (sawmill owner before 2015)
owners.note: Wikipedia says Schweighofer took over the Kodersdorf sawmill from the Klausner Group in 2015; exact date not given.

owners.owner: HS Timber Group (formerly Holzindustrie Schweighofer), owned by Evergreen Privatstiftung
owners.note: Operator HS Timber Services GmbH is a Group company at the sawmill site. The CHP plant is on the sawmill site, so ownership is inferred from the group owning the site. Shareholding of HS Timber Services GmbH itself was not seen (Handelsregister/North Data page did not show it).

issues.summary: Register shows COD 2020-06-04 at 11.104 MWe. HS Timber says it commissioned a second CHP plant at the Kodersdorf sawmill in 2024 (URBAS lists 5.28 MWe, April 2024), so the row may be the first unit or a combined figure; the second unit may be missing from the register.

summary: Bark-fired CHP at the HS Timber sawmill in Kodersdorf, owned by the HS Timber Group, which belongs to Evergreen Privatstiftung; the 2015 sawmill takeover date is the best proxy for owner_since. No financing or operating problems found; the plant-level shareholder chain and the second 2024 CHP unit versus the register row remain unconfirmed.
